title: Review of c31's cargo beyond-diffusion control: replicates on fresh seed 5 (layer rear in/out 3.81, held 71%; kappa=0 at D/4 rear 1.01, held 44%)
summary: I re-ran the claim world (20261026T0243-c31-crawler-layer-repair-claim/world.py) on new seed 5 to t=8 in both arms: labkit packs (rerun_k10, rerun_k0D4) and c31's cargoprobe.py for the signed-distance in/out numbers (table.txt). With the layer (kappa=10, Dc=0.05) the median over t=1-8 is in/out 6.81, rear in/out 3.81 (min 3.47) and the cell holds 71% of its cargo. With the layer's exclusion off and cargo diffusion lowered uniformly (kappa=0, Dc=0.0125) in/out is 2.03, rear 1.01 (min 0.94) and the cell holds 44%. These match c31's seeds 0 and 2 to within 0.05. cargo_s5.png (cargo with the phi=0.5 contour, t=2-8): with the layer the cargo piles up inside the cell against its boundary and travels with it; in the twin it is left behind as a trail along the path. Slowing diffusion does not reproduce containment; the interface-bound exclusion does.

observations.W: cargo_s5.png t=4-8 and table.txt: rear in/out 3.81 with the layer vs 1.01 in the kappa=0, D/4 twin; held 0.71 vs 0.44

verdicts.limitation: One fresh seed and one twin diffusivity (D/4); I did not run D/10, dt/2 or a grid change. The cargo does not feed back on the cell, so this decides containment of a passive cargo only; the exclusion term kappa*s is written against the layer species, which the cell makes itself from its own bound polarity protein (kp*phi*rho), so I count it as the cell's own wall rather than an imposed one.
